title: add-kms-activity-heuristics-rbac-timestamp-guardrail
author: Avery Chen
body:
Context: We observed several near-miss alerts where KMS calls were bulk-replayed from an operator account during a misconfigured CI job. Those calls did not violate existing RBAC rules but created an unusual spike of key-usage that complicates billing, audit analysis and can mask real incidents.

Motivation: Introduce lightweight behavioral checks around KMS usage, tighten temporal assertions in RBAC decisions, and strengthen audit integrity to make anomalous activity easier to detect and harder to obscure. This PR introduces three coordinated changes:

1) KMS Activity Heuristics service: a new in-process detector that emits structured signals when tenant/service principal key usage deviates from historical baselines (rate/region/operation mix). Implemented under pkg/kms/activity_detector.go and wired into the KMS proxy path so signals are attached to audit envelopes. Heuristics are intentionally conservative (sensitivity defaults to low) and exposed behind a feature flag (kms.activity_heuristics.enabled) and a tenant opt-in policy.

2) RBAC Timestamp Guardrail: a guard in internal/rbac/timestamp_guard.go that rejects authorization assertions with timestamps more than 5 minutes in the future or a configurable skew. This prevents replay scenarios where actor-supplied timestamps could be manipulated to evade temporal constraints. The guard integrates with the policy evaluator and adds a clear audit tag (rbac.timestamp_guard.hit=true) when triggered.

3) Audit Integrity Fence: audit writer now appends a lightweight HMAC to each audit envelope (services/audit/hmac_writer.go) computed with a rotation-aware signing key from the existing KMS-backed keyring. The HMAC is validated by the audit-forwarder and exposed as audit.hmac_verified=true/false in the console for quick triage.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged behind kms.activity_heuristics.enabled and rbac.timestamp_guard.enabled.
- Default: heuristics disabled, timestamp guard enabled for operator-scoped tokens only.
- Canary: enable heuristics for 10% of internal tenants, collect signals and false-positive metrics for 2 weeks.
- Full rollout after meeting false-positive target (<0.5%) and pager burden sign-off.

Backwards compatibility:
- Audit HMAC is additive and optional; older forwarders will ignore the header but a migration job (scripts/migrations/audit_hmac_backpopulate.sh) is included to backfill HMACs for recent windows when possible.
- Timestamp guard has a permissive mode (rbac.timestamp_guard.mode=permissive) that records but does not reject to aid rollout.

Testing:
- Unit tests for heuristics thresholds and timestamp boundary behaviour (pkg/kms/activity_detector_test.go, internal/rbac/timestamp_guard_test.go).
- Integration tests exercising KMS proxy path with synthetic burst patterns (e2e/security/kms_heuristics_e2e.test).
- Manual verification steps listed in the checklist below.

Operational runbooks:
- docs/runbooks/kms-heuristics.md: how to interpret signals, tuning knobs for sensitivity and lookback window.
- docs/runbooks/audit-hmac-verification.md: how to validate HMACs and troubleshooting rotation errors.

Security review:
- Threat modeling added (docs/security/threatmodels/kms-activity-heuristics.md) that covers poisoning and false-positive risks.

Linear/Jira: linked to ENG-14022 (detect anomalous key-usage), SEC-517 (audit integrity initiative).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Feature flags implemented
- [x] Runbooks and docs written
- [x] Security review completed
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Migration notes: No mandatory tenant migration. Script included to backfill HMACs where KMS envelope data exists. If any service opts-out, heuristics signals will not be emitted for that tenant.

Related work: This complements earlier RBAC and KMS-region controls by adding behavioral signals and temporal hardening rather than broad deny rules. See ENG-9081 for prior regional KMS gating work.
